issues.description: Eleanor framing Josh's trust as a strategic advantage reads like an investigator executing a plan. Should sound predatory (exploiting vulnerability) not investigative (using trust to extract information).
issues.fix: He trusts me completely. That makes him vulnerable.
issues.rationale: Shifts from investigator language ('using trust to get information') to predator language ('trust equals vulnerability to exploit'). Maintains the ominous tone while avoiding investigation framing.

issues.line_text: Tonight will be different. Tonight I'll find out what I need to know.
issues.description: 'Find out what I need to know' is classic investigator language seeking answers/evidence. Predators don't seek informationΓÇöthey seek opportunities to harm.
issues.fix: Tonight will be different. Tonight I'll push him further.
issues.rationale: Changes from seeking information (investigator) to escalating manipulation (predator). Maintains ominous tone without revealing Eleanor's true investigative purpose.

issues.line_text: That fear makes him vulnerable. Easier to reach. Easier to control.
issues.description: 'Easier to control' is fine predator language, but 'easier to reach' sounds like building investigative rapport rather than exploiting weakness.
issues.fix: That fear makes him vulnerable. Easier to exploit. Easier to control.
issues.rationale: Replaces 'reach' (which implies connection-building for information gathering) with 'exploit' (pure predatory intent). Maintains parallel structure while avoiding investigator framing.

issues.line_text: I came here with a purpose. Instead, I'm losing myself. Every time we're together, I forget a little more what I came here to do.
issues.description: 'What I came here to do' combined with earlier 'find out what I need to know' creates an investigative mission frame. Should read as violent intent being undermined by feelings.
issues.fix: I came here to destroy him. Instead, I'm losing myself. Every time we're together, I forget a little more why I wanted to.
issues.rationale: Changes from mission/purpose language (investigative) to explicit violent intent (predatory). The shift to 'wanted to' (past tense desire) shows feelings eroding her resolve without revealing investigation.

issues.line_text: The time has come. He trusts me completely. He'll believe whatever I show him. I have to be ready to finish this.
issues.description: 'He'll believe whatever I show him' implies presenting evidence/information (investigator revealing findings). Should sound like exploiting trust for harm, not revelation.
issues.fix: The time has come. He trusts me completely. He won't see it coming. I have to be ready to finish this.
issues.rationale: Removes 'show him' (evidence presentation) and replaces with 'won't see it coming' (predator advantage). Maintains ominous intent without investigative framing. Echoes her earlier phone call line for consistency.

issues.line_text: Things I couldn't let go of. Things that proved I wasn't imagining this. All the pieces of a puzzle I'd been circling for so long.
issues.description: 'Pieces of a puzzle' is explicit investigative language. This directly reveals Eleanor is solving a mystery rather than planning violence.
issues.fix: Things I couldn't let go of. Things that fed the anger. All the pieces of what drove me here.
issues.rationale: Removes puzzle/investigation metaphor entirely. Replaces with emotional/vengeful motivation (anger, being driven) which reads as predatory obsession rather than investigative work.

issues.line_text: Because I'd kissed him. Let him inside me. And if something's wrong with himΓÇöif he's not who he seemsΓÇöwhat does that make me?
issues.description: 'If something's wrong with him' reads like uncertainty/investigation. Eleanor is 85% certain Josh is the killer before he arrives (per Story Bible). She should be certain, not questioning.
issues.fix: Because I'd kissed him. Let him inside me. And if I'm falling for the man I came here to destroyΓÇöwhat does that make me?
issues.rationale: Removes investigative uncertainty and replaces with moral conflict about her violent intent versus developing feelings. Maintains her certainty while showing the emotional complication.

issues.line_text: endless acres of frozen wilderness and too many unanswered questions.
issues.description: 'Unanswered questions' frames Eleanor as seeking information (investigator). She should already be certain, with the conflict being execution not discovery.
issues.fix: endless acres of frozen wilderness and too much time to second-guess myself.
issues.rationale: Removes 'unanswered questions' (investigative uncertainty) and replaces with self-doubt about her resolve. Shows internal conflict without suggesting she's still gathering information.

issues.line_text: There was what I knew: Something's wrong with him. He loses time. Forgets things. The cracks are showing, and soon he won't be able to hide what he really is.
issues.description: 'Won't be able to hide what he really is' is investigator language watching for exposure/revelation. Per Story Bible diagnostic: predators watch for FEAR, not exposure. This is the exact pattern fixed in Session 6.
issues.fix: There was what I knew: Something's wrong with him. He loses time. Forgets things. The cracks are showing, and soon he won't be able to resist what's inside him.
issues.rationale: Changes from watching for exposure (investigator) to watching for the danger to manifest (predator observing threat escalation). Maintains observation of Josh's fugue states without framing Eleanor as seeking revelation.

issues.line_text: But I had to keep trying. Had to see this through.
issues.description: 'Keep trying' implies investigative effort to find answers. Eleanor should be preparing to act, not investigating.
issues.fix: But I had to keep going. Had to see this through.
issues.rationale: Subtle change from 'trying' (seeking/investigating) to 'going' (continuing on a set path). Maintains determination without suggesting ongoing investigation.

issues.line_text: Because I couldn't let it go. Couldn't stop. Not until I knew for sure.
issues.description: 'Not until I knew for sure' reveals Eleanor is still investigating/confirming. Per Story Bible, she's already 85% certain and becomes 100% certain during the blackout scene (Ch16+). In December, she should already be certain enough to act.
issues.fix: Because I couldn't let it go. Couldn't stop. Not until this was finished.
issues.rationale: Removes investigative uncertainty ('knew for sure') and replaces with completion language ('finished'). Shows obsession with seeing her plan through, not gathering evidence.

issues.line_text: This was my penance. This was my purpose. This was the only thing that mattered.
issues.description: 'Penance' has grief/justice connotations (making amends, atoning) which could hint at Eleanor's sister connection. Should sound like obsession/vengeance without justice framing.
issues.fix: This was my obsession. This was my purpose. This was the only thing that mattered.
issues.rationale: Changes 'penance' (grief/justice language that hints at personal loss) to 'obsession' (predatory fixation). Maintains intensity without hinting at Eleanor's true motivation.

issues.line_text: I watched him the way I always watched him nowΓÇösearching for signs of whatever I'd seen that morning. Any hint of wrongness.
issues.description: 'Searching for signs' is investigative observation. Should be watching for vulnerability/opportunity (predator) not evidence gathering.
issues.fix: I watched him the way I always watched him nowΓÇöwaiting for the wrongness to surface again. Any hint of what he tries to hide.
issues.rationale: Changes from active searching (investigator) to passive waiting (predator watching prey). 'What he tries to hide' maintains menace without framing Eleanor as evidence-gathering.

issues.line_text: on all the questions I still couldn't answer, all the things that didn't add up
issues.description: 'Questions I couldn't answer' and 'things that didn't add up' is explicit investigative language suggesting Eleanor is still puzzling things out.
issues.fix: on all the ways I was losing control, all the feelings I couldn't afford
issues.rationale: Removes investigative framing entirely. Replaces with emotional conflict about her plan being compromised by feelings for Josh. Maintains tension without revealing investigation.

issues.line_text: Not until I understood what really happened. Why I'd come to Thornewood in the first place.
issues.description: Final line reveals Eleanor is seeking understanding (investigative goal). Directly contradicts that she already knows Josh is the killer and came to confront him.
issues.fix: Not until I finished what I came to Thornewood to do. Why I'd trapped us here together.
issues.rationale: Removes 'understood what happened' (investigation) and replaces with completion of violent intent. 'Trapped us here together' is predatory action consistent with her luring him to the estate.

notes: This chapter has systemic spoiler protection issues. Eleanor's internal monologue consistently uses investigative language (questions, understanding, finding out, pieces of a puzzle) when it should use predatory language (destroying, finishing, exploiting). The sexual content is fine and serves misdirection. The phone call with her mother is excellent misdirection ('made my peace', 'when it's done'). But Eleanor's private thoughts need complete reframing to sound like violent obsession rather than investigation. This is the exact 'recognition-watching' pattern that was fixed in Session 6, appearing here in different forms.
